chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Sa'id al-A'raj who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the fasting person, does he taste something and not swallow it? He said: No. And this does not contradict the earlier reports, because this narration is understood as referring to one who has a need for that, because the concession (rukhsah) was only revealed in that case when there is a compelling necessity leading to it, such as the spoilage of food, or the death of a child, or the death of a bird. As for when all of those are absent, then it is not permissible in any case.
ai.seo_question: Can a fasting person taste food without swallowing it according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that tasting food while fasting is permissible but restricted to cases of genuine necessity, such as checking for spoilage or feeding a child, thereby harmonizing this report with earlier hadiths that assumed a context of need. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle of *rukhsah* (concession) applied specifically to the cook or taster, distinguishing between mere tasting and swallowing, and emphasizing that without such necessity, the act is prohibited.
